perspective:
Gloria Bangura has access to the following:

- She knows Donald Ortega as a colleague who works part-time as a bartender at company events.
- Over several company events, she directly observed Donald’s distracted demeanor and lack of enthusiasm while serving drinks.
- She approached him and asked if everything was okay with his job.
- Donald told her he was “just not as into it as I used to be” and that the job was “kind of repetitive.”
- After that, she began to suspect that his job dissatisfaction might reflect larger personal issues.
- She suggested he consider talking to a professional about it.
- Donald said he hadn’t considered that and wasn’t sure it would help.
- She then sensed a change in Donald’s behavior toward her and worried he might resent her suggestion as an overstep.
- She apologized, saying she wanted to help because she cared and didn’t mean to overstep.
- Donald told her he was “a bit taken aback at first” but knew she meant well and that it was “a lot to process.”
- She felt relieved that the tension had eased and wanted to strengthen their professional relationship.
- She told Donald about an upcoming project and invited his creative input.
- Donald thanked her, said he appreciated it, wanted to be more involved, and called it a great opportunity.
- After they collaborated successfully, Gloria observed Donald’s significant contributions and renewed enthusiasm.
- She concluded he was a valuable team member and publicly acknowledged his work in a team meeting.
- In the meeting, she told the team that Donald’s efforts were crucial to their success.
- Donald thanked her, said the recognition meant a lot to him, and said he was glad to contribute and felt great to be appreciated.
